concerns.text: T003b [P] creates `.gitignore` excluding `data/raw/*.csv`. This violates the data-flow dependency: T004 (checksumming) and Constitution Principle III require `data/raw/` files to be tracked and checksummed. Excluding them in Phase 1 prevents the downstream checksumming workflow from functioning, creating a hard ordering violation where the consumer (checksum logic) cannot access the producer (raw data files).

T014b [US1] explicitly instructs to 'Remove any logic to switch regression families'. This contradicts the data-flow dependency established in T014a (which detects outcome type) and the requirement in FR-003 (which mandates family selection based on that type). T014b destroys the artifact (outcome type logic) required by T021a (model fitting), creating a consumer-before-producer violation where the model task cannot execute its required logic.

T023c-CI-Validate depends on reading `ci_width_warning_threshold` from `code/simulation_parameters.json`. However, T000b-SimulateParams (the producer of this file) and Phase 0 do not define or calculate this threshold. The consumer (T023c) requires an artifact key that the producer (T000b) never emits, causing a runtime dependency failure.

T023b-SimulationValidation and T023c-CI-Validate depend on T023. T023 only extracts coefficients/p-values. The CI width (needed for T023c) and parameter recovery logic (needed for T023b) are not produced by T023. The consumers (T023b/c) require data artifacts (CI bounds, injected effect comparison) that the producer (T023) does not generate, creating a missing-data dependency.

T025b [US2] references `contracts/model_output.schema.yaml` for validation, but T024b-SchemaDef only defines `contracts/model_config.schema.yaml`. The consumer (T025b) depends on a schema artifact that the producer (T024b) does not create, creating a missing-file dependency.
